summary.text: Matt Marshall is a Republican member of the Washington House of Representatives, representing District 2-Position 2 since January 13, 2025, and is on the ballot for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A U.S. Army veteran, he works as a physician assistant and adjunct professor.

paragraphs.text: Matthew Marshall was born in Seattle, Washington, and served in the U.S. Army from 2004 to 2017.

He earned an associate degree in medical laboratory from George Washington University and a bachelor's degree in biology and a master's degree in physician assistant studies from the University of Nebraska Medical Center.
His career experience includes working as a physician assistant and an adjunct professor.

In a 2020 Ballotpedia survey, Marshall said he was born and raised in Washington, lived in unincorporated Pierce County with his family, began as a resident firefighter and emergency medical technician intern in Oregon after high school, and then spent 12 years on active duty in the Army, including two tours to the Middle East.

He said he later helped found a nonprofit called The Three Percent of Washington, was elected a precinct committee officer and then vice chair of the Pierce County 2nd Legislative District Republicans, and was elected to the Eatonville School Board in November 2019.
Marshall won the District 2-Position 2 seat in the November 2024 general election, defeating fellow Republican John Snaza with 55.4 percent of the vote.
In the 2026 general election he faces Democrat Angela Taylor.
